content.text:
The image provided shows a histological cross-section of an umbilical cord. Normally, the umbilical cord contains three vessels: two umbilical arteries and one umbilical vein. In the provided image (`MM-1390-a.jpeg`), only two vessels are visible (one artery and one vein), a condition known as a **single umbilical artery (SUA)** or two-vessel cord.

While a single umbilical artery can be an isolated finding, it is strongly associated with various chromosomal abnormalities when other malformations are present. Among the chromosomal conditions, **Trisomy 18 (Edward syndrome)** is the most frequently linked condition to a single umbilical artery, followed by Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome). Research indicates that approximately 50% of fetuses with Trisomy 18 have a single umbilical artery, whereas the association is less frequent (though still significant) in Trisomy 13, Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), and Turner syndrome.

The correct chromosomal condition most frequently linked to these histological findings is Edward syndrome.

A
